## Finding

For `*p = value; return *p;` with `p` a pointer to a volatile object, the compiler returns `value`
and emits no read. This was reproduced for mcs51. The reporter also observed it for ds390, stm8,
z80, and mos6502, which were not tested for this report.

## Cause

`cseBBlock` in `src/SDCCcse.c` calls `findPointerSet` for reads through a pointer. When
`findPointerSet` finds an earlier store through that pointer, `cseBBlock` turns the read into an
assignment of the value that was stored. Both functions test volatility with `isOperandVolatile`
on the pointer operand. For a pointer type, `isVolatile` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` returns
`DCL_PTR_VOLATILE`, which says whether the pointer itself is volatile. The type that the pointer
points to is not examined.

## Fix

`findPointerSet` returns 0 when the read goes through a pointer to a volatile type. It also
ignores stores whose pointer operand points to a volatile type.

## Verification

The patch adds no regression test. In the simulator setup of the regression suite, a read after
the store returns the value that was stored, so a test cannot distinguish the read from its
replacement.

The assembly for mcs51 was inspected with the patch. Reads through `__xdata` pointers and generic
pointers to volatile follow the store. Two consecutive reads stay two reads. For pointers to
non-volatile objects the compiler forwards the value, as it does without the patch. No other port
was inspected.
